messages.author: 2710b717e5dbb066
messages.subject: Re: Newby ignorance: how is the best way to create multiple plots on one screen?
parts:
The par(mfrow... and layout methods are for base graphics only.  The ggplot2 package (of which qplot is part) uses grid graphics and as you have seen, base graphics and grid graphics don't play nicely together without extra work.

If you call the plot (or print) function explicitly for ggplot objects then you can specify a viewport to use (the default just clears the screen and starts a new set).  So you can do something similar to using layout (but with more control) by first creating your own viewports, then passing that information to the plot/print method for qplot.  Here is a simple example (stealing the actual plots from ?qplot):

library(grid)
library(ggplot2)

pushViewport( vp1 <- viewport(x=0,y=0, width=0.4, height=1, just=c(0,0)) )
upViewport()
pushViewport( vp2 <- viewport(x=1,y=1, width=0.6, height=1, just=c(1,1)) )
upViewport()

plot( qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars), vp=vp1 )
plot( qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars, colour=cyl), vp=vp2 )
On Wed, Sep 11, 2013 at 6:54 PM, Tim Smith <timden...@gmail.com> wrote:

I tried to use par(mfrow.... and layout, but qplots would take over the entire screen. Thought I saw something about that in Wickhan's ggplot2 book, but can't find it.

Any guidance?
Tim Smith

messages.author: c5246646595bff41
messages.subject: Re: Newby ignorance: how is the best way to create multiple plots on one screen?
parts:
Note that the function require the grid package and uses grid() functionalties like:
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(nrow(layout), ncol(layout))))

It might get you what you want for a simple layout but grid(0 and gridExtra() will open a whole new set of possibilities when the space dedicated for each plot is different ( along the layout() function in basic graphics).

David

I would go with Ista's suggestion and do some reading on how to use faceting. http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/facet_grid.html

You will also have to use reshape2 to reformat your data (I am guessing).  This will take a little time for you to get the hang of but once you master it, it will be invaluable.
